fact: The Sunday Times reports that through the SA Connect programme government is expanding broadband infrastructure, public Wi-Fi access and connectivity to households, schools and healthcare facilities, particularly in underserved communities.
USAASA said the minister approved the Universal Service and Access Fund manual, which governs funding interventions meant to strengthen connectivity in underserved communities.

The Witness reports the British High Commission launched on 25 August 2026 a multi-million-rand project supporting community network operators to extend affordable internet to rural and township KwaZulu-Natal, welcomed by the provincial Cogta MEC.

fact: The communications department says Sentech and Broadband Infraco, set to deploy 32,055 Wi-Fi hotspots, have already installed more than 11,500, focusing also on rural and underserved areas.

fact: Minister Gungubele said the SA Connect flagship, which aims to connect 5 million rural and township households, had to date reached 361,000 households through 2,502 Wi-Fi hotspots.
Minister Gungubele says the SA Connect programme has connected over 740,000 rural and township households through 4,250 Wi-Fi hotspots.

MyBroadband reports SA Connect, launched by government in 2013 through Broadband Infraco and SITA, plans 1,180 km of further fibre in Phase 2 to cover about 5.5 million households, with rollout limited by Infraco's finances; its CEO named it and the Broadband Access Fund as key projects in February 2025.

Parliament's communications committee adopted the DCDT's R2.6 billion 2026/27 budget, whose focus includes expanding broadband to underserviced areas, particularly rural communities, townships and public institutions.
